bindings.caption: E. tef grains were washed repeatedly with distilled water. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

E. tef grains were ground into a fine powder. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

E. tef powder was mixed with de-ionized water. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

The solution was heated in a hydrothermal reactor. temperature: 200 °C. duration: 6 h. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

The reactor was cooled to ambient temperature. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

The supernatant was filtered through 0.2 μm PTFE syringe filters. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

The NP-CQDs were dialyzed in pure water for 48 h. duration: 48 h. Recipe-level reported vessel: hydrothermal reactor. No vessel assignment is made for this step. Conceptual action diagram. Arrows indicate an action only; no apparatus detail is inferred.

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
